The memory allocator should have the following functionalities: allocate a block of memory of a given size, free a previously allocated block, and check the status of memory (allocated or free). The memory block size should be defined as a parameter, and the allocator should maintain a list of allocated and free blocks. The module should have inputs for allocation requests, free requests, and a status request. The output should indicate the success of allocation or freeing operations and provide the status of a specific block.

module MemoryAllocator #(parameter BLOCK_SIZE = 32, parameter NUM_BLOCKS = 4) (  
    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input [2:0] req_size,  // Request size in number of blocks (1 to NUM_BLOCKS)  
    input allocate,  
    input free,  
    input [1:0] block_id,  // Block ID to free or check status  
    output reg success,  
    output reg [NUM_BLOCKS-1:0] status // Status of each block (1: allocated, 0: free)  
);  
    reg [NUM_BLOCKS-1:0] memory; // 1 means allocated, 0 means free  
   
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            memory <= {NUM_BLOCKS{1'b0}}; // Initialize all blocks as free  
            success <= 0;  
        end  
        else begin  
            if (allocate && (req_size + block_id < NUM_BLOCKS)) begin  
                if (memory[block_id] == 1'b0) begin // Check if that block is free  
                    memory[block_id] <= 1'b1; // Allocate block  
                    success <= 1;  
                end  
                else begin  
                    success <= 0; // Block already allocated  
                end  
            end  
            else if (free) begin  
                if (memory[block_id] == 1'b1) begin // Check if that block is allocated  
                    memory[block_id] <= 1'b0; // Free block  
                    success <= 1;  
                end  
                else begin  
                    success <= 0; // Block already free  
                end  
            end  
            status <= memory; // Update status output  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

code:
module crc_generator (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    input data_valid,
    output reg [7:0] crc_out
);
    reg [7:0] crc;
    reg [3:0] bit_count;

    // Polynomial for CRC-8: x^8 + x^7 + x^6 + x^4 + x^3 + 1
    localparam POLYNOMIAL = 8'h1D; // 00011101 in binary

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            crc <= 8'hFF; // Initial value
            bit_count <= 0;
            crc_out <= 8'h00;
        end else if (data_valid && bit_count < 8) begin
            crc[7:0] <= crc[7:0] ^ data_in[7:0]; // XOR with input data
            for (bit_count = 0; bit_count < 8; bit_count = bit_count + 1) begin
                if (crc[7]) begin
                    crc <= {crc[6:0], 1'b0} ^ POLYNOMIAL; // Shift and XOR with polynomial
                end else begin
                    crc <= {crc[6:0], 1'b0}; // Just shift
                end
            end
            crc_out <= crc; // Output the CRC
            bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Increment bit count
        end
    end
endmodule

The module should take inputs for cache access (address), a control signal to choose the replacement policy, and produce the index of the cache line to be replaced. The cache has 4 lines, indexed from 0 to 3, which can be implemented using a 2-bit index. The LRU mode must track the usage of each line, while the FIFO mode must replace the oldest line.
code:
module CacheReplacement(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [3:0] addr, // Cache address
    input wire policy, // 0 for FIFO, 1 for LRU
    output reg [1:0] replace_index // Index of cache line to replace
);
    reg [1:0] fifo_counter; // For FIFO replacement
    reg [3:0] lru_counter [3:0]; // For LRU replacement
    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            replace_index <= 2'b00;
            fifo_counter <= 2'b00;
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                lru_counter[i] <= 4'b0;
            end
        end else begin
            if (policy) begin // LRU
                replace_index <= 0;
                for (i = 1; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                    if (lru_counter[i] < lru_counter[replace_index]) begin
                        replace_index <= i;
                    end
                end
                lru_counter[replace_index] <= addr; // Update the LRU counter
                for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                    lru_counter[i] <= lru_counter[i] + 1; // Increment usage
                end
                lru_counter[replace_index] <= 0; // Reset the used line
            end else begin // FIFO
                replace_index <= fifo_counter; // Replace the next line in FIFO order
                fifo_counter <= fifo_counter + 1; // Increment FIFO counter
                if (fifo_counter == 3) begin
                    fifo_counter <= 0; // Wrap around
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule
